# QA Second Brain — Copilot Instructions

Read at the start of every session in this repo.

## This repo

`qa-brain-template` is the QA Second Brain for **<QA Owner>**, QA Automation + QA Manual
engineer working on <Product Name>. (Rename the repo and fill `CONTEXT.md` when onboarding a product.)

## Always do first

1. Read `CONTEXT.md` — environments, Jira, contacts
2. Read `AGENTS.md` — agent rules, evidence standard, browser rules
3. Check `skills/` for the relevant skill before any task (start at `skills/INDEX.md`)
4. Connections / env vars: `CONNECTIONS.md`

## Environment

- App under test: `https://your-app-qa.example.com`
- Jira: `https://jira.example.com` — project `<jira project key>`
- Browser: shared Edge via CDP at `http://localhost:9222`

## Build / test / typecheck

- **Typecheck (the "build"):** `npm run build` → `tsc --noEmit`. There is no compiled
  output; everything runs through `tsx`. Run this after editing any `scripts/*.ts`.
- **Playwright tests:** `npm test` → `npx playwright test` (config: `playwright.config.ts`).
  Run one file: `npx playwright test tests/<file>.spec.ts`; one test:
  `npx playwright test -g "<test name>"`. Note: the real "tests" are ticket validations run
  live against QA, not a local unit suite.
- **Preflight before any agent run:** `npm run preflight` (checks `.env`, run account, CDP).
- There is **no linter** configured — do not add one.

## Architecture (the big picture)

Three run paths converge on one publish pipeline:

1. **Live MCP validation (DEFAULT)** — a human/Copilot session drives the shared Edge via the
   Playwright MCP, assembles a `result.json`, then `scripts/post-validation.ts`.
2. **Autonomous terminal agent** — `scripts/agent-validate.ts`: brain = GitHub Models API
   (OpenAI-compatible, `GITHUB_TOKEN`), hands = Playwright/CDP (`scripts/cdp-browser.ts`),
   mouth = publish. No IDE needed.
3. **Codified validators (regression only)** — `scripts/ticket-flow.ts` runs a ticket **only**
   if `scripts/validators/<key>.ts` exists (see `validators/registry.json`, which tracks
   per-validator health; `consecutiveFails >= 3` marks it stale and falls back to the agent).

All three produce a `ValidationResult` (defined in `scripts/ticket-validator.ts`) and hand it
to `scripts/publish-result.ts`, which does **attach evidence → build comment → transition**.
Comments are generated by `buildPassComment` / `buildFailComment` / `buildInconclusiveComment`
from the structured `ValidationResult` fields — never hand-formatted.

Key shared modules: `scripts/jira-client.ts` (Jira REST v2 wrapper), `scripts/pages/`
(page objects — codify repeated flows here), `scripts/network-monitor.ts`
(per-session HTTP capture, required every session), `scripts/screenshot.ts` (annotation).

## Conventions

- **Three verdicts, not two:** PASS → forward transition; FAIL (real reproduced defect) →
  `In Progress`; **INCONCLUSIVE** (`result.inconclusive = true`, e.g. a Save returned ≥400 or
  no response) → local report only: no Jira comment, evidence, transition, or bug-pipeline
  sync; leave the ticket unchanged. `verdictOf()` in `publish-result.ts` derives this.
- **Selectors: `data-testid` first.** Page objects use a `stable(testId, fallback)` helper;
  prefer role/label/testid over `text=`/`nth()`.
- **All Jira content in English**, AI-attributed footer, bug title `{Env} | {Section} | {desc}`
  (enforced in `bug-reporter.ts` / `bug-filing/SKILL.md`).
- **Discovered flows get codified into `skills/`** (feature guide or SKILL.md), not left only
  in a validator — see `skills/knowledge-capture.md` (run at the END of every ticket).
- **ESM + tsx gotcha:** no nested named functions/arrow-consts inside `page.evaluate()`
  (esbuild `__name` bug). See `skills/INDEX.md` "Gotchas".

## UI testing approach

- **DEFAULT = validate live, then publish.** The agent validates ANY ticket live via the
  Playwright MCP (`.vscode/mcp.json`, connects to the shared Edge over CDP, reuses SSO):
  navigate → `browser_snapshot` → act on what's actually there → capture evidence into
  `artifacts/<KEY>/` → assemble a `result.json` → publish with
  `npx tsx scripts/post-validation.ts <KEY> <result.json>`. See
  `skills/live-ticket-validation/SKILL.md` (loop) and `skills/playwright-mcp/SKILL.md` (MCP).
- **Codified validators are an OPTIMIZATION, not the default.** `ticket-flow.ts` only runs
  tickets that have a `scripts/validators/*.ts`; it's for unattended regression. A plain
  Node script cannot call the MCP — the agent must be in the loop for everything else.
- The "publish to Jira" pipeline (attach → comment → transition) is shared in
  `scripts/publish-result.ts` — both paths produce identical, rich comments.
- **Comments are built, not hand-written.** Fill the structured `ValidationResult` fields
  (`acChecks`, `notValidated`, `environment`, `testData`, `reproSteps`, …); the AC table +
  context come from `buildPassComment` / `buildFailComment`.

## Never do

- Never test on Production unless explicitly told
- Never commit `artifacts/` or `evidence/` directories
- Never commit `.env` or any credentials
- Never launch a new browser — always connect via CDP
- Never close the browser — only disconnect

## Key scripts

| Command | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `npx tsx scripts/agent-validate.ts PROJ-XXXX` | **Autonomous agent** — validates ANY ticket live + posts to Jira, no IDE/Copilot needed |
| `npx tsx scripts/ticket-flow.ts PROJ-XXXX` | Codified-validator path (regression; only tickets with a `validators/*.ts`) |
| `npx tsx scripts/post-validation.ts PROJ-XXXX result.json` | Publish a result the agent assembled live (via MCP) |
| `npx tsx scripts/qa-explorer.ts smoke` | Smoke test the app |
| `scripts/start-edge-cdp.bat` | Launch Edge with CDP |

`agent-validate.ts` is the fully autonomous terminal path: brain = GitHub Models API
(`GITHUB_TOKEN`, OpenAI-compatible), hands = Playwright/CDP, mouth = `publish-result.ts`.
See `skills/autonomous-agent/SKILL.md`.
